title: Upload -> Storage -> ingest_jobs -> LLM extraction pipeline (Gemini Flash primary, native-PDF-text fast path)
goal: Every uploaded receipt gets an ingest_jobs row and is parsed by Gemini Flash into structured, Zod-validated line items within the <30s p95 target, without a synchronous wait blocking the upload response.
in_scope: ingest_jobs row created (state='queued') immediately after S-05's receipts row, in the same Server Action

Background processing via Next.js `after()` (next/server) — the upload response returns immediately (working spec Journey 2: 'upload should return instantly'); the LLM call and everything downstream runs in the same function invocation's extended lifetime, not a separate round trip or new infra (tech-stack.md: 'no separate job queue')
LlmProvider interface (lib/llm/provider.ts) wrapping Gemini Flash — a one-file swap per working spec Sec7, even though only one implementation exists today

Cost fast path for PDFs: try native-text extraction (pdf-parse) first; if yield looks like a real document (>200 chars, currency marker, digit-heavy lines) send text-only to Flash; otherwise rasterize and go multimodal. HTML/MHTML: extract visible text directly (already textual, same cost principle) and send text-only — not explicitly named 'native-PDF-text' in the working spec but a direct extension of the same reasoning, flagged here rather than silently assumed. Images (JPG/PNG/WEBP, HEIC already converted to JPEG by S-05): always multimodal

Zod response schema exactly as working spec Sec7: merchant, purchased_at, currency, order_total, document_type, lines[] (raw_text, item_name, brand, quantity, unit, pack_size, unit_price, line_total, category_slug, is_non_inventory, confidence)
category_slug constrained to the actual leaf category slugs seeded in S-02 (59 values), injected into the prompt as an enum — the model must not invent a category
Prompt rules: mark tax/fee/discount rows is_non_inventory=true; ignore UI chrome in screenshots (status bars, nav, promo banners); return null rather than guess, never invent a price

On successful validation: write receipt_lines rows (matched_item_id left null — canonicalization/matching is a later epic), update receipts (merchant, purchased_at, total_amount, parse_model, parse_path, parse_tokens, parse_cost), ingest_jobs.state='done'

Per-receipt token/cost accounting written to receipts.parse_tokens/parse_cost (working spec Sec7 cost control — the 100/day hard-stop counter itself is a later story, this just captures the per-call numbers it will need)
Structured logging keyed on receipt_id across upload -> job -> model call (07-infrastructure.md observability requirement)
out_of_scope: Pro-tier escalation retry and manual-entry fallback on failure (S-07)
Canonicalization / line matching to catalog_items (E-3) — matched_item_id stays null here
Review queue UI (E-4) — this story only needs receipt_lines to exist with correct data, not a screen to review them on

The 100/day hard-stop guard itself and the nightly stuck-job-recovery cron scan (working spec F3's 'decided post-consolidation' note) — both need infrastructure (the recompute cron) that doesn't exist yet; ingest_jobs' state machine (queued/processing/done/failed, attempts column) is built so a later story can add the scan without a schema change, but the scan itself is not this story's job
acceptance: A photographed grocery bill extracts >=85% of lines correctly (A1); native-text PDFs take the cheap text-only path, verifiable via parse_path (A22).
invariants: Never auto-commits — parsed lines land in receipt_lines for review, nothing writes to stock_movements or catalog_items from this pipeline (working spec F3)
GEMINI_API_KEY is server-only, same pattern as SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (server-only import guard)

A failure anywhere in extraction must leave the ingest_jobs row in an inspectable, non-silent state (state + error column) — never a swallowed exception with no trace, even though the retry/escalation logic itself is S-07's job
blocked_on_credential: GEMINI_API_KEY — cannot be generated by the agent, must come from the user (Google AI Studio or Vertex AI)
